title: Foreign-player origins in the Chinese Super League: Spatiotemporal patterns and origin-country characteristics associated with registration counts
content:
by Zijie Li, Maoteng Cheng, Fugao Jiang

This study examined the spatiotemporal evolution of foreign-player origins in the Chinese Super League (CSL) from 2010 to 2024 and the associations between origin-country characteristics and foreign-player season registration counts. Longitudinal spatial analyses showed that CSL foreign-player origins extended across multiple continents, while registrations remained concentrated in a limited number of major origins. The spatial extent, weighted centre, and orientation of the origin distribution varied across seasons, but no persistent neighbouring spatial clustering was identified. Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood regression analyses further showed that broader international destination reach and higher fee-weighted Hub values were positively associated with CSL registration counts. Geographic distance, economic-development distance, and the FIFA men’s world ranking score were not statistically significant in the full specification. The registration-count difference between Asian Football Confederation (AFC) member origins and other origins was larger during the period in which the region-specific registration condition applied. Period comparisons provided no statistical evidence of systematic differences in the Breadth or Hub associations across the three historical periods. Overall, the CSL combined broad geographic sourcing with substantial concentration in major origins, while variation in registration counts was associated with origins’ international market reach, fee-weighted Hub values, and the region-specific registration environment.
